stops.note: active participle of afta, "to give a legal decision"
stops.meaning: Islamic legal scholar who issues rulings

stops.note: borrowed to describe the official head of Islamic religious law
British army slang extended the word to "plain clothes," jokingly likening off-duty dress to a mufti's robes
stops.meaning: civilian clothes worn instead of uniform

current_meaning: civilian clothes worn by someone who normally wears a uniform; historically, an Islamic legal scholar
